$comment: Git branches through a family recipe book. Facts checked with git 2.54 in a throwaway repo.

title.text: Git branches: a bookmark, not a copy
title.subtitle: Try an idea without touching what works

sections.label: Analogy: the family recipe book

turns.says: I want to try the soup with chili.
Not in the book we all cook from!
I'll use my own bookmark and new pages.
Fine. If it's good, we keep the pages.

sections.intro: Nobody copies the book. They agree on this:
rules: each new page says which page came before it
a bookmark only marks the page you are on
good soup: the new pages join the family book
bad soup: throw the bookmark away

sections.text: A branch is the bookmark: a name that points at one commit. Creating it copies no files.

rows.a: one written page of the book
rows.b: **commit**: a snapshot of all files + a link to its parent(s)

rows.a: a small strip that marks a page
rows.b: **branch**: a movable name pointing at one commit
`main`, the usual name of the default branch

rows.a: the bookmark you are working from
rows.b: **HEAD**: points at the branch you are on

items.note: HEAD just names the branch you are on.
The whole branch: one commit ID. (Git may also pack refs into one file.)

items.heading: New bookmark
items.text:
`git switch -c feature`
new branch here, HEAD moves to it

items.heading: Write pages
items.text:
`git add .`
`git commit -m "chili"`
the bookmark moves on

items.heading: Back to family
items.text:
`git switch main`
files return to main's snapshot

items.heading: Join the pages
items.text:
`git merge feature`
main now has the chili

items.heading: Drop the bookmark
items.text:
`git branch -d feature`
refuses if unmerged; `-D` forces

sections.label: Merge, case 1: fast-forward
sections.head: main
sections.text: Main had nothing new: `main` just slides to chili. No new commit.

sections.label: Merge, case 2: a merge commit
sections.head: main
sections.text: Both moved on: a new commit with **two parents**. See it: `git log --graph`
Both sides changed the same lines. Git marks them with `<<<<<<<` and waits for a human to choose.
A branch is a bookmark on a commit, not a copy of your files. Make them freely, merge the good ones.
